assessment_summary: I validated the OpenProject Docker all-in-one installation by inspecting the runtime state (not just files) and probing the live application. (1) Container: `docker ps`/`docker inspect` confirmed the named container `openproject` is Up on openproject/openproject:17, with the exact image digest from the summary, port mapping 8080→80, and env vars/mounts identical to the guide's production one-liner (host name localhost:8080, HTTPS=false, language en, generated SECRET_KEY_BASE, pgdata+assets bind mounts). (2) First-run behavior: container logs show the guide's expected messages "Seeding admin user" and "default admin credentials are login: admin, password: admin". (3) Web tier: HTTP requests to http://localhost:8080 returned 302→/login and a 200 sign-in page; the JSON REST API answers in correct OpenProject error format. (4) Internal components: postgres accepts connections (pg_isready), and the process list shows the full all-in-one stack (supervisord, postgres, apache2, Puma with 2 workers, memcached, hocuspocus, background worker, postfix). (5) Data: the DB is seeded (admin user with admin flag, 2 projects) and persists in /var/lib/openproject (80MB PG17 cluster + assets). (6) Credentials: the guide documents default admin/admin. A web form login returned 422 "A new password is required", so I investigated rather than assume failure: the stored hash check via `rails runner` showed check_password?("admin")=true and a wrong password=false, and the source (User.try_authentication_for_existing_user in /app/app/models/user.rb) proves the force_password_change flag is evaluated only after the password check passes. So admin/admin is the valid seeded credential, and the prompt is OpenProject's intended first-launch security flow, not an installation defect. No installation, repair, or configuration changes were made by me; all DB queries were read-only. Limitations: I did not exercise the post-login UI beyond the sign-in flow (changing the seeded admin password is a user action and would count as a configuration change, so I deliberately did not perform it), and the API basic-auth 401 reflects OpenProject v3's session-based API auth rather than a fault. Overall, objective evidence shows the software is installed per the guide, complete, and operational.
